OSG saves $30,000 a year on FX fees with WorldFirst

The Singapore container builder pays its suppliers in China and Vietnam from one World Account, with FX fees down around 40% and payments reaching suppliers 35% faster.

OSG sells, leases and converts shipping containers into site offices, event spaces, pop-up shops and sanitary facilities. Founded in Singapore in 2006 and now run by brothers Andrew and Adam Aw, it has sold more than 100,000 containers to more than 1,000 business customers.
  • Industry
Automotive & Industrial
  • Location
Singapore
  • Company size
11 to 50 employees
35%

60%

40%

Introducing OSG: flexible space on demand
OSG buys shipping containers, converts them into offices, event spaces, pop-up shops and sanitary facilities, and sells or leases them to more than 1,000 business customers. The company started in Singapore in 2006 with something the founders' father noticed after the 1997 Asian financial crisis. He came from construction, and he could see containers sitting idle in yards while businesses paid heavily for temporary space.
His sons, Andrew and Adam Aw, run the business now. More than 100,000 containers have left the yard since. Singaporeans walk past many of them today without a second look: Artbox booths, National Day Parade facilities, sites run by PSA, DHL, and Samsung.
OSG sources containers and components from suppliers in China and Vietnam, and supports projects in Malaysia, Australia, Indonesia and the US. Every one of those suppliers wants to be paid in their own currency, and most want to be paid before the work starts.
Making cross-border transactions was a big issue. Payments often took days to process with limited visibility on their status. They also included high foreign exchange rates and fees that added to our operational costs.
Andrew Aw
OSG
The challenge: payments that couldn't keep up with the containers
A construction company orders a site office for the start of a job. OSG needs that container in its yard weeks beforehand, which means paying the supplier in Guangzhou or Ho Chi Minh City weeks earlier again. The only issue they had was getting the money to the supplier on time.
No one could see where a payment was
Bank transfers took days to clear, and once a payment left the account the team had no way of following it. They knew it had gone. They could not tell a supplier when it would arrive, and suppliers will hold production until the money lands. Each transfer took 20 to 30 minutes to make, then more time again to answer questions about its location and time of arrival.
Bank fees and moving rates added to cost every container
Banks charged on each international payment, and the exchange rate moved between quoting a job and paying for the steel behind it. OSG was already absorbing rising material costs to keep its prices steady for customers, so every dollar lost at the payment stage came out of the same margin.

WorldFirst Business

Open the account OSG runs on. Hold 20+ currencies and get cashback on card spend.

The solution: one account for every currency OSG buys in

WorldFirst, a brand of Ant International, gave them one account, the World Account, to receive, hold, convert and pay in the currencies it trades in.
Suppliers paid in their own currency, tracked the whole way
OSG pays its Chinese suppliers in CNH and others in USD, straight from the account. Batch payments settle several suppliers in one run rather than one transfer at a time, and real-time tracking shows where each payment has reached. When a supplier asks, the team has the answer on screen, and the factory starts cutting steel sooner.
Conversion and card spend in the same place
Money sits in the account in Singapore dollars and converts when the rate suits OSG rather than when a bank gets round to it, so the cost of a container stays close to the cost quoted for it. Smaller international spend goes on the World Card, which OSG also uses with suppliers who take card payments, and the card earns cashback on everything that runs through it.
The result: money that moves at the pace of the builds
Payments now happen in the background while the team gets on with the builds. Here is what that has been worth to OSG:
35%
faster supplier payments
Money reaches China and Vietnam sooner, so production starts sooner
60%
fewer payment delays
Real-time tracking replaces the wait for a bank to confirm anything
40%
lower FX fees
Conversion happens inside the World Account rather than at bank rates

SGD$30,000 saved a year: money that goes back into stock, people and projects

20 to 30 minutes saved per transaction: one account, one run, nobody chasing a status
SGD$1,000 in cashback a year: earned on World Card spend, plus SGD$2,000 a year in FX fees removed from card payments
By switching to WorldFirst, OSG has freed up both money and hours, and both are going into growth: digital marketing, better inventory monitoring, and the daily work of moving hundreds of containers around a yard and on to happy customers.
OSG sells, leases and converts shipping containers into site offices, event spaces, pop-up shops and sanitary facilities. Founded in Singapore in 2006 and now run by brothers Andrew and Adam Aw, it has sold more than 100,000 containers to more than 1,000 business customers.
